rows.meaning: from one side to the other
rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone or something moves from one side to the other.

example.english: We’ll go across and wait for you over there.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gwo3 heoi3 go2 bin1 dang2 nei5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose pattern for moving from one side of an area or object to the other.

example.english: We go across the bridge to the other side.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gwo3 tiu4 kiu4 heoi3 go2 bin1

rows.note: Use this for something being located on the other side rather than moving across.

example.english: The convenience store is across the street.
example.jyutping: bin6 lei6 dim3 hai2 deoi3 min6

rows.note: Use this locative pattern when something is on the opposite side of a street, river, or other divider.

example.english: The convenience store is across the road.
example.jyutping: gaan1 bin6 lei6 dim3 hai2 maa5 lou6 deoi3 min6

rows.jyutping: waang4 fong3 hai2 A soeng6 min6
rows.note: Use this when an object is laid crosswise over another object, especially in an instruction.

example.english: Lay the wooden stick across the table.
example.traditional: 將條木棍橫放喺張枱上面。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 tiu4 muk6 gwan3 waang4 fong3 hai2 zoeng1 toi4 soeng6 min6

rows.note: Use this pattern when something occurs throughout an entire area rather than moving across it.

example.english: Music could be heard across the whole housing estate.
example.traditional: 成個屋邨都聽到音樂聲。
example.jyutping: seng4 go3 uk1 cyun1 dou1 teng1 dou2 jam1 ngok6 seng1
